title: Round 7 / ECDLP-21: partial-agreement lower bounds for the EC discrete-log map
question: If a polynomial or low-degree rational function f on E agrees with the discrete-log map k (mod p) on a delta-fraction of {kP : 1 <= k <= N}, what lower bound on deg f follows (curve analogue of Coppersmith–Shparlinski / Lange–Winterhof partial-agreement results)? Give exact statements, proofs or proof attempts, literature status, and toy-curve checks.

sources.title: Coppersmith, Shparlinski, On polynomial approximation of the discrete logarithm and the Diffie-Hellman mapping, J. Cryptology 13 (2000) 339-360 (bibliographic data only; full text not accessed)
Lange, Winterhof, Interpolation of the elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman mapping, AAECC-15, LNCS 2643 (2003) 51-60 (citation only)
Lange, Winterhof, Polynomial interpolation of the elliptic curve and XTR discrete logarithm, COCOON 2002, LNCS 2387, 137-143 (citation only; Lange publication list)
Kiltz, Winterhof, Polynomial interpolation of cryptographic functions related to the Diffie-Hellman and discrete logarithm problem, Discrete Appl. Math. 154 (2006) 326-336 (citation only)
Kelley, Meka, Strong bounds for 3-progressions, FOCS 2023
Shparlinski, Cryptographic Applications of Analytic Number Theory, Birkhauser 2003

claims: Proof attempt (Theorem 1): for r prime, N<min(p,r), f regular at kP and f(kP)=k mod p on A subset [1,N], deg f >= T_j(A)/2 for every 1<=j<=N-1 where T_j=#{k:k,k+j in A}; hence deg f >= m(m-1)/(4(N-1)) ~ delta^2 N/4 for any A of size m=delta N, and deg f >= ((2delta-1)N-1)/2 for delta>1/2; polynomial f in X,Y of total degree d has d >= deg f/3.

Proof attempt (Theorem 2): for r odd prime, N<=(r-1)/2, g in F_p[X] of degree d with g(x(kP))=k^2 on A: d >= S_j(A)/3 for every j (S_j = # 3-APs with difference j in A); recovers Theorem B for A=[1,(r-1)/2]; d >= ((3delta-2)N-2)/3 for delta>2/3; for any fixed delta>0, d >= c(delta)N for N>=N_0(delta) conditional on cited Varnavides/Kelley-Meka counting results.

Experimental (toy, p<100): 48 random-subset cases and structured subsets show no violation; true minimal degrees ~ m (polynomial) and ~ (m+1)/2 (rational, two-section construction) so the proved delta^2 N/4 is not tight for sparse subsets, nearly tight for intervals.
Remark: hypothesis j not 0 mod p (N<p) is necessary: constant f agrees with k mod p on a residue class when N>p.
next_action: Independent review of Theorems 1-2 and Cor. 1c/2b; obtain full texts of Coppersmith-Shparlinski and Lange-Winterhof to settle novelty; attempt to close gap between delta^2 N/4 and (delta N+1)/2; Lean formalization of the translate lemma (Theorem 1) if prioritized.
